configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line AB in the order A-C-D-B. C is the midpoint of AB so AC = CB. D is between C and B, so CB = CD + DB and AD = AC + CD = CB + CD. The entire proof operates algebraically on lengths and areas (rectangles and squares) derived from this linear configuration. No auxiliary points are constructed off the line.
pass_reason: The proof is essentially algebraic, applying Props 2.1, 2.3, and 2.4 as algebraic identities to lengths on a line. The only spatial claims concern the collinear ordering A-C-D-B, which is consistently maintained in every step. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no ray orderings — nothing that could produce a spatial configuration contradiction.
